title: A foundational atlas of autism protein interactions reveals molecular convergence
authors: Wang B; Vartak R; Zaltsman Y; Naing ZZC; Hennick KM; Polacco BJ; Bashir A; Eckhardt M; Bouhaddou M; Xu J; Sun N; Lasser MC; Zhou Y; McKetney J; Guiley KZ; Chan U; Kaye JA; Chadha N; Cakir M; Gordon M; Khare P; Drake S; Drury V; Burke DF; Gonzalez S; Alkhairy S; Thomas R; Lam S; Morris M; Bader E; Seyler M; Baum T; Krasnoff R; Wang S; Pham P; Arbalaez J; Pratt D; Chag S; Mahmood N; Rolland T; Bourgeron T; Finkbeiner S; Swaney DL; Bandyopadhay S; Ideker T; Beltrao P; Willsey HR; Obernier K; Nowakowski TJ; Hüttenhain R; State MW; Willsey AJ; Krogan NJ
one_liner_zh: 该文构建自闭症相关蛋白互作网络并利用AlphaFold-Multimer预测直接互作，虽涉及转录因子FOXP1的DNA结合位点重配置，但核心是蛋白-蛋白互作而非TF-DNA结合建模，方法上仅部分使用结构预测，与课题关联有限。
abstract:
Summary

Translating high-confidence (hc) autism spectrum disorder (ASD) genes into viable treatment targets remains elusive. We constructed a foundational protein-protein interaction (PPI) network in HEK293T cells involving 100 hcASD risk genes, revealing over 1,800 PPIs (87% novel). Interactors, expressed in the human brain and enriched for ASD but not schizophrenia genetic risk, converged on protein complexes involved in neurogenesis, tubulin biology, transcriptional regulation, and chromatin modification. A PPI map of 54 patient-derived missense variants identified differential physical interactions, and we leveraged AlphaFold-Multimer predictions to prioritize direct PPIs and specific variants for interrogation in Xenopus tropicalis and human forebrain organoids. A mutation in the transcription factor FOXP1 led to reconfiguration of DNA binding sites and altered development of deep cortical layer neurons in forebrain organoids. This work offers new insights into molecular mechanisms underlying ASD and describes a powerful platform to develop and test therapeutic strategies for many genetically-defined conditions.
abstract_zh:
摘要

将高置信度（hc）自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）基因转化为可行的治疗靶点仍难以实现。我们在HEK293T细胞中构建了一个涉及100个hcASD风险基因的基础蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络，揭示了超过1,800个PPI（87%为新型）。这些相互作用因子在人脑中表达，并富集于ASD而非精神分裂症的遗传风险，汇聚于涉及神经发生、微管生物学、转录调控和染色质修饰的蛋白质复合物。一个包含54个患者来源错义变异的PPI图谱识别出差异性的物理相互作用，我们利用AlphaFold-Multimer预测来优先筛选直接PPI和特定变异，以便在热带爪蟾（Xenopus tropicalis）和人前脑类器官中进行验证。转录因子FOXP1中的一个突变导致DNA结合位点重排，并改变了前脑类器官中深层皮层神经元的发育。这项工作为ASD背后的分子机制提供了新见解，并描述了一个强大的平台，用于开发和测试多种遗传定义疾病的治疗策略。
